Article Title: Midterm blues: Why a 'lame' duck Donald Trump may push for a quick India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. (Image for representative purpose only)

What this means for India-US trade deal

What does Democrats’ win in US midterm elections mean for India-US trade deal prospects? Will Donald Trump be forced to change his strategy?The unfavourable midterm election outcome is unlikely to prompt President Donald Trump to change course on trade, according to an analysis by Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).But, it’s important to note that both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and the strengthening of supply chains.Democratic lawmakers, too, favour protective tariffs to safeguard unionised workers and local industries.“The adverse midterm results won’t change President Donald Trump’s trade direction because both Democrats and Republicans now favor economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing, and strong supply chains,” says Ajay Srivastava, founder of GTRI.Unable to rely on Congress for every measure, Trump is expected to continue exercising powers already available to the administration. These include Sections 232 and 301, along with executive orders, Treasury sanctions and rules issued by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), to exert unilateral pressure on trading partners.According to GTRI, with foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win.“Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout,” he says.For several months, leaders on both sides have indicated that a trade agreement is close to being finalised. However, the lack of clarity over the US offer appears to have held up its completion, the think tank says.Trump is now likely to use his executive authority to push India towards an early agreement that opens up the Indian market to American agricultural and industrial products, while securing other significant concessions for US businesses.The agreement under negotiation between India and the US is fundamentally different from the other free trade agreements (FTAs) India has entered into. Under conventional trade agreements, both participating countries reduce or eliminate their regular import duties, which are governed by World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and referred to as Most Favoured Nation (MFN) tariffs.The proposed US–India framework, however, follows a different approach. Washington would continue to levy its regular MFN duties, while India would be required to eliminate or lower such tariffs on most industrial products and a wide range of agricultural goods.The February 6 US–India Joint Statement sets out further commitments for India. These include aligning its security and economic policies with Washington, purchasing $500 billion worth of American goods over five years, and relaxing domestic regulatory oversight of imports from the US.“The US may be relying on the threat of additional tariffs to secure India's compliance. These include potential measures linked to India's purchases of Russian oil under the Graham Act and Section 301,” Srivastava notes.Also, signing the agreement would not necessarily protect India from further tariff action. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion.“India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement. Opening its markets, committing to large purchases and limiting its policy choices would carry lasting costs, while any U.S. tariff relief could prove temporary. New Delhi should insist on clear, enforceable reciprocal concessions, consistency with WTO rules and full freedom to protect its energy security and development priorities. The pressure to announce a deal must not outweigh the need to secure one that serves India’s long-term interests,” Srivastava says.
Article Summary: Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion. India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement.

Article Title: Elon Musk's nearly $500 million US midterm gamble backfires: Tesla, SpaceX stocks take a hit
Article Text:
Musk's political gamble falls flat, Tesla, SpaceX stocks take a hit

Why Musk's businesses could feel the political heat

Where Musk's $474 million election money went

Musk was not the only tech billionaire backing Trump

Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the US midterm elections, but lost the gamble. As Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress and Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure.Shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure, with SpaceX falling 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipping 3.6%. Both stocks underperformed the broader market.The decline came even as US equities rallied following the midterm elections. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, gaining 119.7 points to close at 7,688.62. The Nasdaq Composite added 364.50 points, or 1.4%, to 25,736.51, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,569.40 points, or 3%, to 53,356.12. The Dow rose more than 1,500 points during the session.US stocks have historically tended to gain following midterm elections, regardless of which party wins. However, Musk's businesses moved in the opposite direction as the election results dealt a blow to the Republicans and US President Donald Trump, a close ally whom the billionaire helped elect.The setback is particularly significant given Musk's business interests in Texas, which houses his electric vehicle maker Tesla, his rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.His election spending was aimed at helping Republican candidates retain their positions and keeping Texas red.An analysis by The New York Times suggests that Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates during the 2026 midterms, including almost $224 million in Texas alone, making him the biggest donor of the election by a considerable margin.The Democratic victory could have significant implications for Musk's companies, particularly SpaceX's plans to build data centres. Slower approvals for these facilities could become a major hurdle as the company looks to tap the $28.5 trillion addressable market it presented to investors ahead of its IPO.With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, analysts and experts expect greater scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible pushes for construction moratoriums amid growing local opposition over electricity costs.Musk has already faced scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers over restrictions on satellite communications used by Ukraine, mass federal job cuts at DOGE, and government contracts and subsidies flowing to his companies. The stronger Democratic presence in Congress could bring these issues back into focus.The latest market reaction also comes after a strong recovery in Tesla shares. The stock has rallied 34% since its late-July low, supported by investor optimism surrounding its artificial intelligence products and the potential combination with SpaceX.SpaceX, meanwhile, entered the ranks of the world's most valuable companies after going public earlier this year. The company generates billions of dollars through US government contracts, but its shares have largely remained flat since its June IPO, holding on to a massive $1.9 trillion market valuation.Musk's companies have previously shown sensitivity to election outcomes. Following Trump's re-election in 2024, Tesla shares surged more than 90% in little over a month. However, those gains later unwound as Musk's relationship with Trump soured and investors grew tired of his involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency.A significant portion of Musk's election spending flowed through political action committees supporting Republican candidates across the country.His America PAC, the super PAC he owns, received $216 million and was active in more than 40 House and Senate races. According to Newsweek, Musk contributed another $77 million to the group in the first half of October alone.The Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC backing Senate Republicans, received $168 million. Of this amount, $158 million was passed on to Texas PAC, the biggest supporter of Republican Ken Paxton.Musk also contributed $30 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund to help protect the Republican majority in the House. His trust gave another $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, the main outside group supporting Paxton.His involvement in Republican fundraising is not new. In 2024, Musk spent nearly $300 million backing Trump and other Republican candidates.Musk's political contributions were the largest among four technology billionaires who backed Trump. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, Michael Dell and Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff also supported the president through financial contributions, charitable commitments and White House projects.Ellison contributed around $45 million to a nonprofit supporting Trump's 2024 campaign, according to The Wall Street Journal. The donation remained undisclosed until June 2026. He later praised Trump at the White House event announcing the Stargate AI project, telling him, "We certainly couldn’t do this without you". Trump described Ellison as the "CEO of everything".Michael Dell and his wife Susan pledged $6.25 billion to fund "Trump Accounts". The money will go to the US Treasury and be deposited in $250 amounts into accounts for 25 million children aged 10 or younger. The programme targets children in zip codes where the median income is $150,000 or less. Trump later urged Americans to buy Dell computers, following which the company's stock rose more than 7%.Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff also backed Trump, marking a shift from his earlier political contributions, a major share of which went to Democrats. He committed $1 million towards Trump's White House ballroom, while Salesforce separately made two commitments of $1 million each. Benioff later faced criticism for supporting the deployment of National Guard troops in San Francisco, a proposal opposed by local city leaders. He subsequently withdrew his remarks and apologised for calling in the Guard.
Article Summary: Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the US midterm elections. As Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure. SpaceX fell 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipped 3.6%. Both stocks underperformed the broader market.

Article Title: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows as Trump loses US midterm elections
Article Text:
Crude prices fall below $100 per barrel

Trump faces pressure as war weighs on Republicans

Qatar steps up mediation as Iran deal remains distant

Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90, as markets continued to react to the political fallout of the US midterm elections and the possibility of an end to the war with Iran.Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 a barrel, while WTI crude declined 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.The latest movement follows Wednesday's sharp sell-off, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 a barrel, shedding $8.98 or 8.7%, while WTI settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3%. Both contracts recorded their lowest closing levels since August 31.The market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that US President Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.The election outcome has also complicated Washington's options in the conflict. With Democrats taking control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump could find it harder to pursue further military action.Two sources close to Gulf government circles told Reuters that the weakened political position gave him greater reason to pursue a negotiated settlement, making a full-scale assault on Iran less likely.However, the possibility of a deal does not necessarily rule out further escalation. Gulf analysts said an agreement that allows Iran to claim a clear victory while leaving Trump appearing defeated could encourage recklessness rather than restraint.Trump told the Financial Times earlier this week that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. A day later, he acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections.Vice president JD Vance also questioned the decision to enter the war on Wednesday, distancing himself from it and blaming the conflict entirely for the Republicans' electoral setback.Tehran, however, has indicated that a change in political control in Washington would not alter its position towards the US. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that American hostility would continue regardless of which party was in power.There were also fresh developments in the region, with Yemen's Houthis claiming to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.Diplomatic efforts to prevent another escalation have gathered pace, with Qatar stepping up mediation following the US elections. But the prospect of an immediate breakthrough remains uncertain.Meanwhile, regional energy flows continue to be disrupted. The United Arab Emirates is also looking at ways to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, considering a third oil pipeline.Separately, US oil stockpiles recorded a decline last week. The Energy Information Administration said crude inventories dropped by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended October 30. This was sharply different from expectations in a Reuters poll, where analysts had forecast an increase of 877,000 barrels.
Article Summary: Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90. Market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.

Article Title: Trump tariff taxes Republicans: What US midterm results mean for Indian H-1B visa holders, Russian oil & trade deal
Article Text:
American voters have handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party.

The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US - so what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look:

What it means for H-1B visa holders and green card aspirants

India’s purchase of Russian oil

India-US trade deal & tariffs

US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections with Republicans losing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.In a significant rebuke to Trump, American voters on Tuesday handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party and shifted several key gubernatorial positions in closely watched elections.Trump's Republican Party suffered major defeats in its strongholds, including Texas, Georgia and Iowa, losing the governors' offices to Democratic candidates.Trump’s policies are being blamed by many as the reason for the loss - with tariffs and inflation in focus.US President Donald Trump has tightened access to H-1B visas through a $100,000 fee and a wage-weighted selection system, making it harder for Indian professionals to secure US jobs. His administration has also suspended eight technology companies from the PERM green card programme, disrupting some workers’ routes to permanent residency and green cards. So will the midterm results change that attitude?No. Not much is expected to change on this front, despite Trump’s loss. This is because both Democrats and Republicans prioritise domestic employment.According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), tighter immigration policies find bipartisan support.“Be it the Biden administration or the Trump one, policies are increasingly becoming restrictive and that approach is unlikely to change,” Srivastava tells TOI.Also Read | ‘Death by restriction’: As Trump sours H-1B visa dream, which Indian IT professionals face the biggest hit? According to Rajiv Dabhadkar, Founder, National Organization For Software and Technology Professionals, the H-1B debate has moved beyond party politics to a fundamental US policy challenge: protecting American jobs while retaining access to global talent.“Regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections, the US is looking to address long-standing flaws in the immigration system, including wage protections, worker displacement and how employers use foreign professionals,” he tells TOI.What fundamentally needs to be understood is that H-1B reform is now a bipartisan American policy imperative, not merely a political reaction to one administration, he adds.Earlier this year, the Donald Trump administration managed to get support for the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The Act allows the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries importing oil from Russia and Iran in a big way.India and China lead the lot of Russian oil buyers. Recently, Trump announced a waiver on those tariffs for India. But, it’s important to note that the waiver was only for a period of 60 days.Also Read | Does Trump’s 60-day tariff waiver really give relief to India? What it means for US trade deal & oil prices The Republicans losing control of the Congress is unlikely to change the Trump administration’s stance on buyers of Russian crude oil. This is because the bill enjoyed bipartisan support - both Democrats and Republicans appear keen to penalise buyers of Russian oil.However, what may work in India’s favour for now is America’s own diesel deal with Russia and the need by the Trump administration and even the Democrats to keep oil prices in check. Sanctioning Russian oil or penalising buyers of Moscow’s crude will not help that cause.So, for now India continues to enjoy relief from the prospect of 100% tariffs for its crude oil procurement from Russia, but this may work as a pressure tactic by the US to finalise a trade deal.For India, which is still negotiating a trade agreement with the United States, the outcome of the midterm elections could strengthen the case for taking a cautious, wait-and-watch approach.Earlier this month, Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the India-US trade agreement was in the final stages of drafting. However, he stressed that New Delhi would move ahead only if the terms gave Indian exporters an edge over their competitors.India and the US have already finalised a framework for the first phase of the Bilateral Trade Agreement. However, changes in the US tariff environment have led to further negotiations. India is seeking tariff rates on its exports that are more favourable than those faced by competing countries.In the meantime, experts believe the midterm setback could prompt Trump to pursue an early trade agreement with India. They said that with Washington struggling to exercise foreign policy leverage over Russia, China and Iran, Trump may look for quick success on the trade front.However, the economic think tank GTRI said the unfavourable midterm outcome was unlikely to fundamentally alter Trump's trade policy. Both Republicans and Democrats, it noted, support economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and robust supply chains."With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win. Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout and the midterm losses may push Trump to seek a quick India trade deal," said Ajay Srivastava.Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) president SC Ralhan said the US continues to be an important destination for Indian goods and services."What will matter to Indian exporters in the months ahead is how US policy on tariffs and market access takes shape. MSMEs in particular need predictable trading conditions to price orders confidently and plan shipments months in advance," he told PTI.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections. Republicans lost control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US. So what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look.

Article Title: Nifty50 to hit 28,000 in 2027? 3 factors that could drive Dalal street's next run
Article Text:
Stock market outlook: Where is Nifty50 headed?

Foreign investors return as AI-linked trades unwind

Slower AI spending and lower oil prices improve sentiment

Citi raises Nifty's valuation multiple to 18 times

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

NEW DELHI: Dalal Street has had quite a run, clocking its strongest rally in 35 years with Sensex soaring an impressive 10% rise in the pre-Diwali session.But with the celebrations comes the big question: can the stock market keep the momentum going in Samvat 2083, or will investors have to brace for a few bumps along the way?Brokerage firm Citi Research seems to be betting on more upside, raising the Nifty50 target to 28,000 points by the end of 2027, up from its earlier estimate of 26,000 points by September 2027. The new target suggests an upside of around 12% from the index's last close of 24,986.4.The firm has identified three key factors that could support equities in the coming period: a strong earnings outlook, lower crude oil prices and the possibility of slower capital expenditure on artificial intelligence (AI).Citi has also raised the valuation multiple assigned to the benchmark index.The revised target comes after a period in which Indian equities lagged their global peers. Enthusiasm around the AI trade and elevated crude oil prices had weighed on the outlook for Indian stocks, particularly as the country is the world's third-largest oil importer.However, the recent market trend has been more encouraging. The Nifty 50 gained more than 10% over seven trading sessions through Friday, supported by renewed buying from foreign portfolio investors (FPIs). The return of foreign money coincided with an unwinding of AI-linked trades and a retreat in oil prices.Citi believes there could be further room for foreign investment in Indian equities."Over the past two years, AI has crowded out almost everything else. Our analysis suggests a ~100bp increase in India active weight could drive ~$12bn of inflows," Citi said in its India equity strategy note dated November 8.FPIs have already purchased Indian shares worth more than $4.1 billion in November so far. This marks their biggest monthly inflows since September 2024.The shift in investor sentiment towards Indian equities has also followed the Democratic victory in the US midterm elections. This fuelled expectations of slower AI-related capital expenditure and lower oil prices, amid hopes of an end to the conflict involving Iran.Citi said the possibility of a slower pace of data centre investments could encourage investors to move towards other assets, potentially benefiting Indian markets."Post US mid-terms, risks of increased pace of data center moratoriums has aided rotation into other assets, (and this) could continue to benefit India," Citi said.Lower crude oil prices are another factor behind the brokerage's positive outlook. Since India is the world's third-largest oil importer, a decline in oil prices could support its macroeconomic outlook as well as earnings assumptions."Lower oil price could help India's macro and earnings assumptions. A $10 (per barrel) lower oil price would help (current account deficit) by 30-40 bps and inflation by 50 bps," the brokerage firm said.Citi's revised Nifty target also reflects a change in the valuation multiple it uses for the benchmark index. The brokerage has increased its price-to-earnings multiple to 18 times from 17 times, taking its target to 28,000 points by the end of 2027.Its earlier projection had placed the Nifty 50 at 26,000 points by September 2027.The latest estimate therefore reflects both the higher valuation multiple and the brokerage's expectations of support from earnings, lower oil prices and a possible slowdown in AI-related capital expenditure.
Article Summary: Brokerage firm Citi Research seems to be betting on more upside, raising the Nifty50 target to 28,000 points by the end of 2027. The firm has identified three key factors that could support equities in the coming period: a strong earnings outlook, lower crude oil prices and the possibility of slower capital expenditure on artificial intelligence.

NEW DELHI: The Diwali festivities continue, and bank customers in several states will have to plan their branch visits around upcoming holidays.Banks will remain closed on Monday, November 9, with further closures scheduled for November 10 and 11. The holidays will vary from state to state, depending on the festivals being observed, including Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja, Bali Pratipada and Bhai Dooj.Here's a look at the state-wise bank holiday schedule for the rest of November.Banks in Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Chandigarh, Sikkim, Assam, Manipur, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh will stay shut due to Diwali/Laxmi Puja (Deepawali)/Govardhan Puja/Vishwakarma Day.Banks will remain closed in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and Sikkim to mark Diwali (Bali Pratipada), Deepawali, Govardhan Puja, Laxmi Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year Day.Banks in Sikkim, Manipur, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Himachal Pradesh will remain closed for Laxmi Puja, Ningol Chakkouba, Bhartridwitya, Bhai Dooj and Chitragupt Jayanti.Banks in Meghalaya will remain closed on account of the Wangala Festival.Banks in Bihar and Jharkhand will remain closed for Chhath Puja, also known as Surya Shashthi Dala Chhath (Prath Arghya).Banks in Uttarakhand will remain closed to mark Igas-Bagwal.Banks in Meghalaya will remain closed for Seng Kut Snem.Banks will remain closed in Mizoram, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Telangana, Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, Nagaland, West Bengal, Delhi, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Himachal Pradesh on account of Guru Nanak Jayanti, Karthika Purnima and Rahas Purnima.Banks in Karnataka will remain closed to mark Kanakadasa Jayanti.Bank customers need to check the holiday schedule for their state, as closures depend on the regional festival or occasion being observed.Apart from festival-related closures, scheduled and non-scheduled banks also observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month, in line with the Reserve Bank of India's holiday schedule.A branch closure does not mean customers lose access to all banking services. ATMs, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), internet banking and mobile banking applications remain available for routine transactions, including fund transfers, bill payments and account management.The main inconvenience is for transactions that require a visit to a physical branch. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent work may have to wait until their branch reopens.With several holidays scheduled across November, checking the applicable state calendar before visiting a branch can help customers plan their banking requirements and avoid delays.
Article Summary: Banks will remain closed on Monday, November 9, with further closures scheduled for November 10 and 11. The holidays will vary from state to state, depending on the festivals being observed, including Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Bali Pratipada.

Article Title: Global food prices fall in October: Why wheat, dairy and meat are getting cheaper
Article Text:
Global food prices cool

Wheat and maize prices drag down cereal index

Dairy and meat prices also move lower

Sugar bucks the trend, rises to highest level since December 2024

Vegetable oil prices edge higher

Global food prices lost some ground in October, with cheaper cereals, dairy products and meat pulling down the overall index despite a sharp rise in sugar prices. The decline came amid subdued international demand and expectations of higher supplies of some key food commodities, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).The FAO Food Price Index (FFPI), which measures monthly movements in international prices of a basket of globally traded food commodities, slipped to 133.9 points in October 2026. This marked a decline of 1.6 points, or 1.2%, from the revised September reading.However, the easing in prices has not brought the index below its year-ago level. It was still 5.9% higher than in October last year, although 16.4% lower than its record peak of March 2022.Cereals recorded one of the steepest declines among the major food categories. The FAO Cereal Price Index dropped 4.5% in October compared with the previous month.Wheat prices reversed their four-month upward trend, with subdued international demand and an improved production outlook, particularly in Argentina, weighing on prices.FAO said “The FAO Cereal Price Index fell 4.5 per cent from September. World wheat prices declined following four consecutive monthly increases, largely reflecting subdued international demand and an improving production outlook, particularly in Argentina”.Expectations that restrictions on Black Sea export flows could ease also put pressure on wheat prices. However, continuing logistical disruptions in the region prevented a sharper decline.Maize prices also softened after touching a three-year high in September. The progress of harvesting in the United States and expectations of ample supplies from major South American exporters contributed to the decline.Rice was an exception within the cereals category. The FAO All Rice Price Index rose 1.6% during October, as harvest delays in some exporting countries and adverse weather conditions pushed prices higher.The decline extended to dairy products, with the FAO Dairy Price Index falling 1.1% from September.Lower international prices of butter and cheese, supported by ample supplies and subdued buying interest, drove the decline. These movements more than offset further increases in milk powder prices.Meat prices followed a similar trend. The FAO Meat Price Index fell 1.2% during the month, although it remained marginally above its level a year earlier.Prices of pig, ovine and bovine meats declined in October, while poultry meat prices remained broadly stable.Sugar prices continued to move higher even as most other food commodities became cheaper.The FAO Sugar Price Index climbed 6.6% from September and stood 28.8% above its level a year ago. October marked its fourth consecutive monthly increase, taking the index to its highest level since December 2024.Rainfall-related disruptions to sugarcane harvesting and crushing operations in Brazil's key Centre-South region were the main reason behind the increase, FAO said.Concerns about production prospects in India, the European Union and Thailand during the 2026/27 season also added to the upward pressure on prices.The FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index recorded a marginal increase of 0.3% in October.Higher prices of soybean and sunflower oils offset the decline in rapeseed oil quotations, leaving the overall index slightly higher than its September level.In a separate assessment, FAO forecast global cereal production at 2,999 million tonnes in 2026. This would make it the second-highest level on record, although it would remain below the record production level achieved in 2025.Global cereal trade is also expected to contract in the 2026/27 season. Trade volumes are projected to fall 3.3% to 507.7 million tonnes, largely due to an expected 8.6% decline in wheat trade.
Article Summary: Cereals recorded one of the steepest declines among the major food categories. Wheat prices reversed their four-month upward trend, with subdued international demand and an improved production outlook, particularly in Argentina, weighing on prices. The decline extended to dairy products, with the FAO Dairy Price Index falling 1.1% from September.

Article Title: DLF to invest Rs 3,750 cr in JV with Everstone to buy stake in IREO India
Article Text:
DLF has partnered with the Everstone Group to create a joint venture dedicated to investing in IREO India Companies.

Sain

Real estate major DLF and Everstone Group, a Singapore-headquartered global investment manager, will form a JV to invest in IREO pvt ltd and other group companies in India (IREO India Companies) held by the IREO group of FDI funds (IREO Funds), with investments from reputed global investors. DLF intends to invest about Rs 3,750 crore for a majority stake in the JV that will hold economic interest in the IREO India companies. The proposed transaction could deliver developments across Delhi, Gurugram and other regions. On completion, the IREO India companies will be operated by an independent management team under the guidance of DLF and Everstone.The proposed transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including satisfactory completion of due diligence, receipt of all applicable corporate, regulatory and third-party approvals, and execution of definitive documents.Closing is expected to occur during 2027.DLF MD Ashok Kumar Tyagi said: “We are pleased to partner with everstone group on this strategic investment. Bringing together strong industry experience and global investment capabilities, we look forward to unlocking the growth potential of the IREO India Companies.”Everstone group co-founder and CEO Sameersaid: “It’s our privilege to partner with DLF, especially given their incredible capabilities in a market they understand extremely well. Consistent with our fiduciary responsibilities we look forward to working hard and creating significant value for our IREO Funds investors.”
Article Summary: Real estate major DLF and Everstone Group will form a JV to invest in IREO India companies. DLF intends to invest about Rs 3,750 crore for a majority stake in the JV. The proposed transaction could deliver developments across Delhi, Gurugram and other regions.

Article Title: Delhi protests: Traders body consider approaching govt, courts over business disruptions
Article Text:
Many business claimed large businesses losses amid protests

The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) is considering approaching the government and courts to seek restrictions on protests and demonstrations that disrupt commercial activity, amid growing concerns among Delhi's traders over losses caused by repeated political agitations.The traders' body will take up the issue at a national meeting in Delhi on November 13, with representatives of trade organisations from across the country expected to attend. It plans to assess the impact of protests in the capital over the past month and draw up a strategy to prevent similar disruptions in other cities.The dispute has gained momentum following a series of demonstrations in Delhi, including the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan. The opposition parties had gathered to protest alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's voter-roll revision exercise and demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The issue of protest venues has also been contentious. Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as the capital's designated protest site on October 11 and identified Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues.However, trade organisations have raised concerns about Ramlila Maidan because of its proximity to major wholesale markets in Old Delhi, including Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk and Khari Baoli.CAIT has argued that repeated demonstrations, road closures and traffic restrictions affect more than shopkeepers. They disrupt the movement of goods, supply chains, transport services and the livelihoods of employees and small traders. The organisation has said the impact is particularly severe during the festive and wedding seasons, when commercial activity typically picks up.CAIT Secretary General and Chandni Chowk MP Praveen Khandelwal said the organisation would discuss designating suitable locations on city outskirts or other appropriate areas for demonstrations. “The proposed sites would enable peaceful demonstrations while protecting markets, commercial centres, transport routes and essential business activities,” he said, according to a statement.The proposal is aimed at allowing political parties and other groups to exercise their right to protest without affecting the ability of businesses to operate. CAIT has said it wants the arrangement to be considered across the country, rather than being limited to Delhi.The November 13 meeting will also discuss other concerns facing traders, including GST compliance, cyber fraud involving digital payments and the proposed 'One Trader-One Licence' framework. The latter aims to reduce the number of separate licences businesses must obtain from different government departments.CAIT National President B C Bhartia and National Chairman Brij Mohan Agarwal are expected to lead discussions on regulatory changes, simplifying business procedures and strengthening small businesses.The organisation has maintained that the right to peaceful protest must be protected, but should not come at the cost of other citizens' livelihoods and their right to conduct business.
Article Summary: Traders' body will take up the issue at a national meeting in Delhi on November 13. It plans to assess the impact of protests in the capital over the past month and draw up a strategy to prevent similar disruptions in other cities. The dispute has gained momentum following a series of demonstrations in Delhi.

Article Title: India's crypto tax could hurt blockchain innovation: Buterin
Article Text:
Vitalik Buterin

Mumbai: India’s cryptocurrency tax regime could hamper blockchain innovation and undermine the country’s potential to become a hub for building core blockchain infrastructure, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said.Speaking on the sidelines of Devcon, Ethereum’s annual global developer conference, in Mumbai, the 32-year-old Russian-Canadian programmer said the 30% tax on crypto gains and 1% tax deducted at source (TDS) on transfers could disproportionately burden smaller developers and discourage innovation.Buterin pointed to proposals in the US for a de minimis exemption on small-value transactions and tax exemptions in some countries for assets held for over a year. India needs a regulatory framework that allows developers to experiment without excessive compliance burdens, he suggested.He believes India can move beyond supplying developers to global technology companies and become a centre for building blockchain infrastructure. Its large Ethereum developer community, open-technology culture and govt-backed open-source initiatives offer grounds for optimism, he said.Buterin, who proposed Ethereum in 2013 at the age of 19, helped expand blockchain’s use beyond digital currency. The platform, launched in 2015, allows developers to build applications using blockchain technology.“There is a lot of excitement from people who want to build open technology, both inside Ethereum and outside, and we wanted to engage with that,” he said, explaining India’s choice as the venue for Devcon.He also sees scope for blockchain to complement India’s digital public infrastructure, particularly the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and govt services. While UPI has made domestic transfers quick and inexpensive, Ethereum-based applications could facilitate cross-border commerce and automate payments triggered by specified conditions.Buterin cited AnonAadhaar, which uses cryptographic proofs to establish possession of an Aadhaar identity without revealing personal information, as an example of blockchain’s potential to improve privacy in govt-linked services. Zero-knowledge proofs can enable identity verification without disclosing underlying personal data.Artificial intelligence could further accelerate blockchain development by making complex systems easier to understand and coding faster. Buterin said tasks that once took him days to understand could now take as little as 30 minutes. AI-assisted wallet prototypes already allow users to give simple instructions, such as transferring cryptocurrency, while the system works out the steps, he added.The shift of funding and developer attention towards AI may have left the blockchain sector with about a third of the resources it had two or three years ago, he said, but at the same time AI had compressed development timelines previously expected to stretch over five years into two.
Article Summary: Vitalik Buterin says India’s cryptocurrency tax regime could hamper blockchain innovation. He believes India can move beyond supplying developers to global technology companies and become a centre for building blockchain infrastructure. He also sees scope for blockchain to complement India's digital public infrastructure, particularly the Unified Payments Interface.

Article Title: Cheaper Scotch raises stakes for desi whisky
Article Text: BENGALURU: Cheaper Scotch is putting Indian whisky makers under pressure, even as lower import duties offer savings to companies that use it in their blends. For small distillers that make their own spirits, an imported label can now cost substantially less than a locally made bottle.Huli's rice malt whisky was launched in Karnataka at Rs 2,650 for 750ml. By comparison, J&B Rare was priced at Rs 1,375 at Bengaluru retailer Tonique in October, according to TOI's earlier reporting. At these prices, J&B Rare cost Rs 1,275 less, or about half as much. Tonique said the price had fallen from Rs 2,835, attributing the reduction to local bottling."The smaller players will not be able to survive," said Huli Spirits founder Aruna Urs. Her Mysuru distillery makes spirits from locally sourced paddy and jaggery and does not import Scotch.Arun Kumar Parasa of Unistil Alcoblends said falling Scotch prices had adversely affected the Indian single malt industry. Lower duties on bulk Scotch imported by some small and medium distilleries would benefit them "very marginally", he said.The distinction is between making spirits locally and buying imported whisky for bottling or blending.Bulk Scotch arrives in large containers and can be bottled here or used as an ingredient in Indian whisky.A lower import bill can help these manufacturers, while cheaper finished bottles intensify competition for other producers.Jason Holway, senior consultant at drinks research firm IWSR, expects the price gap to narrow further. "Depending on the state, cheaper blended Scotches are expected to become more attractively priced than they used to be and may not be much more expensive than domestic premium brands using Scotch as an ingredient."India's trade agreement with Britain cut Scotch import duties from 150% to 75%. Customs officials subsequently questioned whether certain bulk shipments qualified for the lower duty. On Nov 2, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal assured manufacturers that the duty benefits would be protected, with commerce and revenue officials to work on resolving the classification dispute.An industry executive, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Indian buyers were also negotiating better purchase prices from Scotland. The executive estimated that the duty reduction could lower retail prices by roughly 8-10%, depending on state taxes and companies' pricing decisions. Distribution difficulties and advertising restrictions remained longstanding hurdles for small manufacturers, the executive added.IWSR's figures also show the limits of India's shift towards expensive whisky. Its premium-and-above category, defined as Rs 2,899.01 or more per 750ml bottle, accounted for less than 1% of whisky consumed by volume in 2025, Holway said.
Article Summary: Cheaper Scotch is putting Indian whisky makers under pressure. Lower import duties offer savings to companies that use it in their blends. For small distillers that make their own spirits, an imported label can now cost substantially less. Huli's rice malt whisky was launched in Karnataka at Rs 2,650 for 750ml.

Article Title: Distribution ring-fenced from impact of new Irdai norms: LIC
Article Text:
.

'

IDBI Bank

sale not to have significant impact on business'

MUMBAI: LIC has said it is in an advantageous position under Irdai's new distribution norms and it also has taken steps to ring-fence the performance of bancassurance channels despite the impending sale of IDBI Bank - its largest bank distribution partner. Officials cited low expense ratio, diversified distribution network and declining dependence on IDBI Bank.LIC CEO and managing director R Doraiswamy said the insurer's cost structure gave it an advantage over competitors, even if they reduced distribution costs. "Anybody else reducing the cost of distribution alone will still have to do a lot of work to bring their overall expense ratio to be under that. So, we stand to be on a distinctly advantageous position, and will be closely watching the market as it unfolds," he said in an analysts' call.On the proposed IDBI Bank stake sale, Hemant Buch, executive director, marketing, bancassurance and alternate channels, said LIC did not expect a significant decline in business sourced through the lender. IDBI Bank's contribution has moderated from historical highs to around 20% of LIC's total bank-driven business and about 30% of its bancassurance volume."While IDBI will continue to deliver value for us and remain a valued and esteemed partner, we do not foresee much depletion in terms of their contribution and overall impact on the volume of bancassurance-driven performance," Buch said.He added that LIC was expanding its partnerships with other public and private sector lenders. Govt has recently approved sale of LIC and govt stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax group.Doraiswamy also said product pricing did not depend solely on the total expenses built into a policy. He said competitors relying more heavily on non-agent distribution channels or lower distribution costs would still need to reduce their overall expense ratios to match LIC's cost structure."We would like to protect the interest of our agents in as much as whatever is possible within the regulatory framework, and that is why we have given our specific recommendations on some areas which concern the points raised by the agents' groups as well. We hope that there will be a good discussion, and when the version of draft regulations are released," said Doraiswamy."In last couple of years, in fact, dependence on IDBI has, in fact, moderated. What it used to be around 50% to bank-driven business and almost 40% to total bancassurance business of corporation, it has moderated to around 20% of total and 30% to bank. Further moderation also is, in fact, taking place despite the, in fact, using the fact that IDBI continues to grow, but then, in fact, we also continue to grow with direction coming from, in fact, other partners," said Buch.Irdai's proposed overhaul of insurance distribution, which seeks to sharply cut commissions, tighten expense limits, curb bank-led sales incentives and restrict loan-linked insurance bundling, has triggered resistance from insurers, banks, brokers and agents who fear loss of revenue, jobs and disruption to established distribution models, even as the regulator seeks to curb mis-selling and reduce costs for policyholders.
Article Summary: LIC CEO and managing director R Doraiswamy said the insurer's cost structure gave it an advantage over competitors, even if they reduced distribution costs. Officials cited low expense ratio, diversified distribution network and declining dependence on IDBI Bank. Govt has recently approved sale of LIC and govt stake to Fairfax group.

Article Title: For the first time since 2017, Sensex and Nifty end Muhurat trading in the red
Article Text:
MUMBAI

Electronic receipts for silver, platinum soon?

: For the second time in 10 years, sensex and Nifty both closed lower during the special hour-long trading session on Diwali which marked the start of Samvat year 2083, one of the Hindu calendars which is followed by the Gujarati trading community who dominate the city's share market.In Sunday's low-volatility, low-volume trading session, sensex opened higher at 81,299 points, was up nearly 300 points from its Friday close, touched a high of 81,442 points, and then profit-taking at higher levels pulled it down to below the 81K mark. Finally, it settled at 80,999 points, down 29 points on the day.The last time sensex had closed in the red during Muhurat trading was in 2017. Nifty on NSE also followed a similar trajectory and closed 44 points lower at 24,986 points. For Nifty too, it was the first negative close during the Muhurat session since 2017.The age-old tradition on Dalal Street is that during the Muhurat trading session on Diwali, domestic investors only buy stocks-even if that order is for one stock-and should never sell. So usually during the Muhurat trading session, leading indices close higher, even if with marginal gains. However, there have been exceptions. And, Sunday's session for the start of Samvat year 2083 was one of those rare ones.The day's lower close for these indices came after a seven-session rally that added over 10% to take each of the indices to multi-month high levels. The day's modest consolidation appears to reflect natural profit-booking following an exceptional week of gains, said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. "Rallies of such magnitude rarely sustain their momentum indefinitely without a period of consolidation, and a single symbolic trading hour was unlikely to buck that pattern. "In Sunday's session, while some of the leading large-cap stocks closed lower, pulling the leading indices lower, midcap and smallcap stocks witnessed buying. As a result, BSE's midcap index closed 0.5% higher while the smallcap index closed 1.5% higher. In turn, the aggregate market capitalisation of all the companies listed on BSE jumped by about Rs 2.6 lakh crore with the current figure at an all-time high of Rs 506 lakh crore, exchange data showed.The day saw, going by decades-old tradition, families of brokers, traders and other market players going to the exchanges, participating in Lakshmi Puja at the bourse, and some even putting in symbolic trades.Ashishkumar Chauhan, MD, NSE, said the bourse launched trading in electronic gold receipts (EGRs) on Friday, the day of Dhanteras, traditionally an occasion for buying gold, silver. On the first day itself, over 1.8 lakh EGRs were traded. Chauhan said that in future, similar products could be launched.
Article Summary: sensex and Nifty both closed lower during the special hour-long trading session on Diwali. The last time sensex had closed in the red during Muhurat trading was in 2017. The day's lower close for these indices came after a seven-session rally that added over 10%.

Article Title: Brooklyn tenants rented an apartment from someone falsely claiming to own it, then faced a $120,000 judgment sought by the former landlord; after the building was sold again, a New York court dismisse
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

How the tenants became involved in the ownership dispute

The agreement that led to a $120,000 claim

Why the New York court dismissed the claim

What the ruling means

Renting an apartment from someone who falsely claims to own a property can lead to unexpected legal problems, even for tenants who believe they have a valid lease. In Brooklyn, Deborah and Demetris Jones found themselves facing a $120,000 claim after renting an apartment from a woman who had fraudulently represented herself as its owner. The dispute continued even after the building changed hands, but a New York court has now dismissed the claim, finding that the former property owner no longer had the right to pursue it after selling the building and transferring its legal rights.In a decision issued on November 5, 2026, and dated November 6, 2026, the New York Supreme Court in Westchester County ruled in favour of the tenants in 131 Vernon Elite, LLC v. Jones. The judgment , available on Justia, examined whether a former landlord could enforce an earlier agreement against tenants after selling the property and assigning its rights in a separate landlord-tenant proceeding to the new owner. The court concluded that the former owner could no longer enforce the agreement under these circumstances.Deborah and Demetris Jones moved into Apartment 3 at 131 Vernon Avenue in Brooklyn on February 15, 2018. They had signed a lease with Sepideh Homayoonfar, who falsely presented herself as the property's owner.The ownership dispute was later addressed in a separate court proceeding. A February 28, 2023, decision declared a fraudulent deed that purported to transfer ownership to Homayoonfar's deceased husband invalid.This restored ownership to Shaul Amzalag, who subsequently transferred the property to 131 Vernon Elite LLC on March 29, 2023.Vernon Elite began legal proceedings against residents of the building, including the Joneses, by commencing a holdover proceeding on April 22, 2023. On September 1, 2023, it filed a separate lawsuit seeking $163,000 for use and occupancy from September 1, 2017. The claim included periods before the Joneses had moved in and before Vernon Elite became the property's record owner.On October 30, 2023, Vernon Elite reached a settlement agreement with the tenants. Under the arrangement, the Joneses agreed to vacate their apartment and return the keys by February 18, 2024.The agreement also stated that if the tenants complied with the terms of a separate landlord-tenant settlement, the company would waive outstanding arrears and discontinue its claim against them. However, if they breached the agreement, Vernon Elite could seek a judgment. Before the agreed move-out date, another major change occurred. On February 6, 2024, Vernon Elite sold the building to Abraham Gelbstein and transferred its rights in the landlord-tenant proceeding to him.The Joneses did not leave by February 18. However, on March 29, they reached a new court-approved agreement with Gelbstein, who had replaced Vernon Elite in the landlord-tenant case. Under the new arrangement, the tenants could remain until May 31, 2024, in exchange for two payments of $2,000 for their continued occupancy. The Joneses made both payments and vacated the apartment by the agreed date. Despite the sale and transfer of its legal rights, Vernon Elite continued pursuing its earlier claim. It sought a judgment of $120,000, along with interest and legal costs, based on the previous settlement. A judgment was signed on September 23, 2024.In August 2026, the Joneses, through new legal counsel, asked the court to vacate the judgment. After hearing oral arguments on August 31, the court set it aside and held an inquest on September 17, hearing testimony from a member of Vernon Elite and Demetris Jones. The central question was whether Vernon Elite still had the legal right to enforce the original agreement after selling the property and transferring its rights to Gelbstein.The court explained that ownership of property includes several rights, such as the right to possess it, control it and receive it back when someone occupying it leaves. When Vernon Elite sold the building, it transferred its ownership rights to Gelbstein. This meant that Vernon Elite no longer had the right to demand the apartment keys or take possession of the property when the Joneses were supposed to leave. The court also noted that the company had separately transferred its rights in the landlord-tenant proceeding to the new owner.Gelbstein subsequently negotiated a fresh agreement with the tenants, allowing them to remain for additional time in exchange for occupancy payments. The court found that this new agreement replaced the earlier landlord-tenant arrangement between Vernon Elite and the Joneses. It also rejected the idea that the former owner could continue demanding money based on an agreement connected to possession of a property it no longer owned or controlled.The court noted that Vernon Elite could potentially have protected its financial interests through an arrangement with the buyer when selling the building. However, no such protection was established in the case.It also observed that Vernon Elite had benefited from the original agreement because it was able to sell the property before the tenants' departure date without an escrow being held or credits being given to the buyer because of their continued occupancy. The judgment and order, dated November 6, 2026, dismissed the case, with the court concluding that Vernon Elite no longer had the right to enforce the agreement against the Joneses.The decision highlights how selling a property and transferring associated legal rights can affect an ongoing landlord-tenant dispute. It also shows why the terms of a property sale and the handling of existing tenant agreements can become important when ownership changes during legal proceedings.

They had signed a lease with Sepideh Homayoonfar, who falsely presented herself as the property's owner. Vernon Elite began legal proceedings against residents of the building, including the Joneses, by commencing a holdover proceeding on April 22, 2023. Article Title: In 2016, Jim Carrey bought a Maui oceanfront retreat for $16.5 million; after listing it for $35 million in October 2026, he found a buyer within weeks, though the final sale price is not yet known
Article Text:
The great room features soaring ceilings, exposed wooden trusses and seamless access to a covered outdoor lanai.

Terminates 10 years of ownership

Two houses with a view of the Pacific

A resort at home

A more quiet life away from Hollywood

Another major real estate exit

For nearly a decade, Jim Carrey’s Hawaiian retreat provided him with something Hollywood rarely could- privacy, solitude and the calming presence of the Pacific Ocean. The property is located on just under an acre of prime beachfront land on Maui and is designed to blur the lines between indoor living and the tropical landscape outside. Now the actor looks ready to let go of the stunning estate. Carrey has already sold the property he listed in October 2026 for $35 million, another significant real estate move for the Hollywood star as he enters a new chapter of his personal life.As per Realtor report, Carrey purchased the oceanfront property in 2016 for $16.5 million, said the realtor. His current asking price is $35 million, more than double what he originally paid for it. The Realtor’s property records show that the home is in pending status, which means a buyer is in place, but the amount of the sale has not been released.The property sits on nearly an acre of beachfront land at Keawakapu Beach where South Kihei Road meets the Wailea resort area. The property has approximately 170 feet of ocean frontage, with a wide green lawn and tall coconut palms between the houses and the shore.The estate was designed by architecture firm Ike Kligerman Barkley, with the goal of weaving traditional Hawaiian influences into a sprawling contemporary retreat, states a report by James Edition.Architectural details include thatched roofing, Douglas fir framing, and woven bamboo finishes.The property is 4,717 square feet and was built in 2002, and is spread out over two separate buildings. The main residence has the primary living areas and a main bedroom suite, while a second building provides independent accommodation for guests.The main house has three bedrooms in total across the accommodation of the estate and the guest structure has two further bedrooms with their own bathrooms. The property also has four and a half bathrooms.One of the characteristics is the great room with high ceilings and wooden trusses that create the airy atmosphere. Big openings connect the interiors to a covered stone lanai, allowing residents to flow easily between the inside and outside.The chef's kitchen has two oversized islands, white cabinetry and premium appliances, according to Realtor. The master suite has another unique feature: a swinging bed and floor-to-ceiling windows, and its bathroom features a statement soaking tub and dual vanities.The outdoor spaces are the estate’s biggest attractions. A freeform swimming pool snakes through natural rock formations in between the two buildings. The design features a hidden grotto, a water slide, a shallow lounging ledge and an elevated spa.According to The James Edition, one of the property’s most valuable features is its generous beachfront setting. Its placement allows both buildings to have ocean views and still have a good stretch of landscaped grounds between the residences and the sand.The listing is with Hawaii Life’s Blake Hill and the estate is being sold fully furnished and in excellent condition. "It is an unusual offering in the luxury property market of Maui with its combination of architectural design, privacy and direct beach access."Carrey's relationship with Maui reflects a broader shift in his lifestyle over the past decade. The actor gradually slipped from the limelight into a more private existence after becoming one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in 1994 with films such as Ace Ventura: Pet Detective, The Mask and Dumb and Dumber.James Edition notes that his island routine has mostly involved reading, writing, walking, painting and sketching. Carrey has also expressed his desire to retire from acting and lead a quieter life away from the demands of the entertainment industry.His private life, too, has entered a new phase. The actor recently wed his longtime love, Min Ah, in an intimate Los Angeles ceremony, Realtor reports. The couple have kept their relationship largely private, making the development a major milestone.Carrey’s listing in Maui comes after he sold his longtime estate in Brentwood, Los Angeles. The two-acre property was purchased in 1994 for $3.8 million and was first listed in February 2023 for $28.9 million.According to Realtor, however, it was difficult to find a buyer. After several price cuts, the home finally sold in 2024 for $17 million,Carrey now has a buyer for his Hawaiian retreat and appears to be letting go of another major property. It’s not clear whether he plans to have a home elsewhere in Hawaii or to establish his business in California. Its new owner has a new chapter ahead for the Maui estate, though the final sale price has not been disclosed.Images Courtesy: Instagram/jimcarrey and Realtor
Article Summary: Carrey purchased the oceanfront property in 2016 for $16.5 million. His current asking price is $35 million, more than double what he originally paid for it. The property is 4,717 square feet and was built in 2002. The main residence has the primary living areas and a main bedroom suite, while a second building provides independent accommodation for guests.

Article Title: A North Carolina student went inside a convenience store after a gas pump failed to print his receipt; the $3 Powerball ticket he bought there won him $2 million
Article Text:
Pic credit: NC Lottery

A receipt that changed the course of his life

Five white balls and a Power Play

Life does not always go the way we plan. Sometimes, an unexpected detour can lead to something extraordinary. Bram Dunehew, a college student in North Carolina, had no plans of winning $2 million in the lottery when he stopped to refuel his car. The gas pump failed to print his receipt, sending him inside a convenience store. On a spur-of-the-moment decision, he bought a $3 Powerball ticket, which turned into a life-changing Halloween windfall! “It’s crazy because I never would have even bought that ticket if the receipt had printed outside,” Dunehew told the NC Education Lottery.On Friday, October 30, Bram Dunehew stopped for petrol in Harrisburg. The errand should have taken five minutes. Fill the tank, grab the receipt and drive home. But the pump had other plans. After filling the tank, the receipt didn’t print. So Dunehew, a Concord resident studying civil engineering at college, walked inside Sam’s Mart on N.C. 49 to sort it out.While inside the convenience store, he picked up a $3 Powerball ticket. It was a random decision. Nothing about that purchase was planned or special. Never in his wildest dreams did Dunehew think he would win the lottery that weekend.The printer outside was the only reason he went in at all.The ticket was for Saturday night’s drawing, which fell on Halloween. When the numbers were read, Dunehew had matched all five white balls! He was ecstatic. That alone was worth $1 million. His Power Play option doubled the prize to $2 million!The college student would not have bought the lottery ticket if the gas station’s printer had not malfunctioned. “I think Halloween’s now my favourite holiday. Trick or treating was fun as a kid, but this is insane,” he told the outlet.The odds of winning the Powerball jackpot are 1 in 292 million. Dunehew didn’t hit the jackpot, but the odds still illustrate how rare his prize was. The winners have 180 days from the drawing date to claim their prizes, at the lottery headquarters in Raleigh. After federal and state tax withholdings, he will take home $1,440,201. He plans to use some of the money to buy his father a Cadillac. It is a gift that connects the win to his family, rather than the prize itself.Lottery money has its own story in Cabarrus County, where education programmes received $16 million in lottery support last year. Dunehew’s ticket was a small part of that system, bought on a whim at a counter he only visited because a machine failed.Sometimes these detours take us to places we would otherwise never go. In Dunehew’s case, that detour has brought him a fortune.
Article Summary: Bram Dunehew, a college student in North Carolina, had no plans of winning $2 million in the lottery. The gas pump failed to print his receipt, sending him inside a convenience store. On a spur-of-the-moment decision, he bought a $3 Powerball ticket, which turned into a life-changing Halloween windfall.

Article Title: ‘Will have to return deposits’: Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production, rejects unprofitability claims
Article Text:
Elon Musk pulling the plug on Tesla's Cybertruck

Tesla will have to refund deposits to a large number of customers who placed orders for its Cybertruck pickup, as demand has outstripped the company's production capacity, CEO Elon Musk said. The electric vehicle maker plans to wind down production of the model at its Texas factory in about eight months to make room for its autonomous Cybercab.“We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people,” Musk said in a post on X on Monday, acknowledging that the Cybertruck's order rate was significantly higher than its production rate.Further rejecting unprofitability rumours, he added, "This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production."The latest comments follow Musk's announcement last week that Tesla would add an extra production shift to clear outstanding Cybertruck orders before ending production.The manufacturing line is expected to be shut down around mid-2027, with resources redirected towards scaling up Cybercab output.Musk has rejected suggestions that the decision to discontinue the pickup was driven by profitability concerns. He argued that the complexity of manufacturing the Cybertruck made expanding its production less valuable than using the capacity to build more Cybercabs.“This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production,” he said.Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and began customer deliveries in November 2023. Despite Musk's ambitious sales projections, the pickup has struggled to attract the expected demand. US sales fell 48 per cent to 20,237 units last year, according to Kelley Blue Book, far below Musk's earlier projection of annual sales reaching 250,000 vehicles.The Cybercab, unveiled in October 2024, is a two-seater autonomous electric vehicle designed without a steering wheel or pedals. It is central to Musk's plan to build a robotaxi network and expand Tesla's self-driving ambitions.
Article Summary: Tesla will have to refund deposits to a large number of customers who placed orders for its Cybertruck pickup, CEO Elon Musk said. The electric vehicle maker plans to wind down production of the model at its Texas factory in about eight months to make room for its autonomous Cybercab.

Article Title: US inflation, housing and jobs: 4 key economic updates to watch this week
Article Text:
Inflation, housing and jobs data to set the tone this week

US inflation: October CPI and PPI figures in focus

US housing market: Home sales expected to remain weak

US jobs market: Weekly claims to follow October's job gains

Corporate earnings: CoreWeave, Cisco and SkyDance results due

The US economy faces another important week of data releases, with inflation, housing sales and unemployment figures likely to offer fresh insights into the financial pressures facing consumers and businesses.The focus comes as American households continue to deal with high prices of everyday essentials, from petrol to groceries. The latest updates follow the US midterm elections, in which Democrats swept Congress, a week ago.The economic situation has also been shaped by the war between the US and Iran, which began in February and cut global oil supplies. The resulting rise in energy costs added to inflationary pressures that were already high because of President Donald Trump's unpredictable tariff conflict with much of the world.Economists, investors and policymakers will be watching the upcoming numbers to assess how the war and tariffs continue to affect prices, the housing market and employment.The first major update will come on Tuesday, when the US releases its consumer price index (CPI) data for October. Economists expect inflation to rise to 3.9%, against 3.7% in September.The CPI tracks price movements across a broad range of goods and services.Inflation has remained above 3% since March, following the start of the US war with Iran in February. The conflict led to a sharp rise in energy prices, which pushed up petrol prices and shipping costs.Businesses will also get a fresh reading of their costs on Friday, when the October producer price index (PPI) is released. Unlike the CPI, the PPI measures price changes before goods and services reach consumers.The September PPI report had recorded its biggest increase since December 2022. It also showed how higher fuel costs, particularly for diesel, were feeding into shipping and warehousing expenses.However, crude prices fell sharply over the past week after the US midterm elections. Some believe Democrats, who routed President Donald Trump's GOP, will push to end the Iran conflict, which has sent energy prices soaring.The housing market will be another area of focus, with high property prices and rising interest rates continuing to weigh on homebuyers.The National Association of Realtors will release its October existing home sales report on Thursday. Economists expect the number of previously occupied homes sold to remain largely unchanged from September.The slowdown is not new. Home sales have remained close to an annual pace of 4 million since 2023, well below the historical average of around 5.2 million.Property prices have continued to rise despite the sluggish sales activity. Home prices have recorded annual increases for 39 consecutive months. At the same time, the average interest rate on a benchmark 30-year mortgage is hovering near its highest level in almost three years.Borrowing costs could remain high as the Federal Reserve considers another increase in its benchmark interest rate at its December meeting. The move would be aimed at cooling inflation, which has remained stubbornly high.Employment data will provide another measure of the economy's health. The US is scheduled to release its weekly unemployment claims figures on Thursday.Economists track these numbers because they offer an indication of layoffs and can help assess where the jobs market is headed. The latest weekly data showed that unemployment claims remained at historically low levels.The broader employment market has held up, with US employers adding 165,000 jobs in October. However, there are signs that workers are facing growing pressure.Wage increases have been slow and have not kept pace with inflation, leaving households struggling with the rising cost of living. While layoffs have largely remained in check, workers who lose their jobs are finding it increasingly difficult to secure new employment.Beyond economic indicators, investors will also track a series of corporate earnings announcements for clues about the artificial intelligence industry, data centres and Hollywood.CoreWeave is scheduled to announce its quarterly results on Tuesday, following a difficult week for AI-related stocks. The data centre company is seen by some as more exposed to rising borrowing costs. Its shares dropped close to 20% over the past week.Cisco and Applied Materials will report their results on Thursday.In the entertainment industry, SkyDance is set to post its earnings on Monday. This will be its first earnings announcement since its Paramount studios completed an $81 billion takeover of Warner Bros.
